events.title: Konrad Zuse completes the Z3
events.summary: Konrad Zuse completed the Z3 on May 12, 1941 — the first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer, using electromechanical relays.
events.about: The Z3 read programs from punched film and could perform conditional branching — a stored-program concept years before ENIAC. Destroyed in a 1943 bombing raid, it was rebuilt in the 1960s and is recognized as a Turing-complete machine built for practical calculation.

narrative.whyChosen: The Z3 was the first operational programmable digital computer.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved automatic computation with stored instructions was achievable in wartime Europe.
narrative.problemSolved: Engineers needed repeatable, programmable calculation without manual rewiring for every problem.
